pr_title: Fix Decimal literal formatting in source generators
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/92773

Both ConfigurationBinder and Json were not handling decimal values correctly.  This shares and updates our workaround method for formatting these.

issue_context.title: Configuration Binding Generator Initializes Suffixed Default Values Incorrectly
issue_context.body:
### Description

When configuration binding generation is enabled by means of:

```xml
<EnableConfigurationBindingGenerator>true</EnableConfigurationBindingGenerator>
<Features>$(Features);InterceptorsPreview</Features>
```

…a project can fail to compile with this error message:

```
/app/repro/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder.SourceGeneration/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder.SourceGeneration.ConfigurationBindingGenerator/BindingExtensions.g.cs(87,25): e
rror CS0664: Literal of type double cannot be implicitly converted to type 'decimal'; use an 'M' suffix to create a literal of this type [/app/repro/repro.csproj]
```


### Reproduction Steps

Given the following project file:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <EnableConfigurationBindingGenerator>true</EnableConfigurationBindingGenerator>
    <Features>$(Features);InterceptorsPreview</Features>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting" Version="8.0.0-rtm.23477.9" />
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder" Version="8.0.0-rtm.23477.9" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>
```

…and the following Program.cs:

```csharp
using Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration;

var c = new ConfigurationBuilder().Build();
var x = c.GetSection("Anything").Get<Values>();
Console.WriteLine(x);

readonly record struct Values(int A, string B, decimal C = 2.30m);
```

…run `dotnet build` via SDK version "8.0.100-rtm.23477.37".


### Expected behavior

The compilation succeeds, and the value is bound from configuration.


### Actual behavior

Compilation fails with the following error:

```
/app/repro/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder.SourceGeneration/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder.SourceGeneration.ConfigurationBindingGenerator/BindingExtensions.g.cs(87,25): e
rror CS0664: Literal of type double cannot be implicitly converted to type 'decimal'; use an 'M' suffix to create a literal of this type [/app/repro/repro.csproj]
```

The line in question in the generated code appears here in a method named `InitializeValues` (but really `Initialize{typename}`):

```csharp
decimal C = 2.30;
if (configuration["C"] is string value2)
{
    C = ParseDecimal(value2, () => configuration.GetSection("C").Path);
}
```

### Regression?

I'm afraid I don't know.


### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Configuration

.NET Version: 8.0.100-rtm.23477.37
OS and version: macOS 13.5.1 (22G90)
Architecture: x64
Specific?: No, I don't think so.
Blazor: ❌


### Other information

You know what, I just checked initializing `float C = 2.30f` as well, and it behaves the same.

```csharp
float C = 2.3;
if (configuration["C"] is string value2)
{
    C = ParseFloat(value2, () => configuration.GetSection("C").Path);
}
```

I confirmed this repro in the latest codebase.  We'll need to see what's missing from how we emit the default value.  Thanks for the report @chrisoverzero
I have a fix for this, but in testing it I hit https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/93159.  I'll try to get the fix done for just this case and move on to that next.
@chrisoverzero is this issue blocking your adoption of the source generator in 8.0?  I'm trying to determine if this is worth backporting to our release branch.
It is not blocking me at this time, no. It’s something I discovered when doing reproduction for another issue.
Ok, closing this out for now, the fix will remain in the 9.0 codebase.
While the `decimal` case isn't common, this also fixed the formatting of Enums with default values with is much more common.  We should consider this for servicing.
